You could put connect your ISP's modem to an Ethernet switch then plug your modem and roku directly to the Ethernet switch. Your roku will be connected directly to your modem bypassing your router.

If the roku is WiFi only then would need another WiFi router. The first one connected to the modem is what the roku connects to and has no vpn configured. The second router connects to the first router and that's what you configure the VPN on.
This would create a double nat if I understand what your suggesting couldn't that effect speed.

It could. I've done similar setups for other purposes and never had a noticeable speed drop on the second router. Plus the second one in his setup is running the VPN which would have a speed drop and increase in latency anyway.

This is what I ended up doing. I had a spare Buffalo wireless router with DD-WRT flashed on it. I attach that to the modem, and the roku players attach directly to the Buffalo, while the Asus (VPN) router piggybacks off the Buffalo router. I had to reassign some IP addresses but it works. I'll have to wait and see if the performance drops.
If you're comfortable flashing your router you could put dd-wrt on it then make a VLAN and a secondary WiFi network that goes outside the VPN. That could work too.
